# `spell/known-typo`

**No known typos in comments, docs and prose**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-spell` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-spell` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX, Python, JSON, YAML, TOML, Markdown, CSS, SCSS, HTML |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:spell/recommended` at `warn` · `codelaw:spell/strict` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `auto` — `codelaw fix` applies it; it never changes what the code does |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |

## What it checks

A word in a comment, a docstring, a prose string, Markdown text, HTML text or an HTML `alt`, `title`, `aria-label` or `placeholder`, or a string value of JSON, YAML or TOML is on the pack's list of known typos (`recieve`, `lenght`, `occured`). The fix writes the one correction the list gives, in the word's case.

**Why:** a typo in a message, a doc or a comment reads as carelessness and hides from search (`grep receive` misses `recieve`). The list holds only words that are no English word and come from exactly one common word, so the fix is safe to run unattended.

A string is read only when it holds whitespace and no interpolation; keys are names, not prose. URLs, email addresses, paths, dotted names, hashes, UUIDs, base64, code and identifiers (`snake_case`, `camelCase`, letters and digits mixed) are skipped, as is any word shorter than four letters.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-spell
pip install codelaw-rules-spell
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:spell/recommended` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:spell/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"spell/known-typo" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.js"]
rules = { "spell/known-typo" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"spell/known-typo" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"spell/known-typo" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"spell/known-typo" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "spell/known-typo": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo: <reason>`
- **Python:** `# codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo: <reason>`
- **JSON** has no comments: switch the rule off for the file with a scope, or use the baseline.
- **Markdown:** `<!-- codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo: <reason> -->`
- **CSS:** `/* codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo: <reason> */`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule spell/known-typo --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain spell/known-typo       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule spell/known-typo  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>    # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Run `codelaw fix`: each typo becomes its correction.
2. For a word that is right where it stands (a product name, a quoted misspelling), excuse the line: `// codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo: <reason>`.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js
// Retry until we recieve a response.
throw new Error("Unexpected lenght of the header");
```

#### Do

```js
// Retry until we receive a response.
throw new Error("Unexpected length of the header");
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx
const Hint = () => <p title="Wrong lenght">Retry untill it works</p>;
```

#### Do

```jsx
const Hint = () => <p title="Wrong length">Retry until it works</p>;
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts
// The adress is checked first.
const message: string = "No adress given";
```

#### Do

```ts
// The address is checked first.
const message: string = "No address given";
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx
const Empty = (): JSX.Element => <p>Nothing recieved yet</p>;
```

#### Do

```tsx
const Empty = (): JSX.Element => <p>Nothing received yet</p>;
```

### Python

#### Don't

```python
def parse(data):
    """Return the adress of the first record."""
```

#### Do

```python
def parse(data):
    """Return the address of the first record."""
```

### JSON

#### Don't

```json
{ "description": "Checks the lenght of a name" }
```

#### Do

```json
{ "description": "Checks the length of a name" }
```

### YAML

#### Don't

```yaml
# Runs untill the queue is empty.
summary: Clears the cache untill the next run
```

#### Do

```yaml
# Runs until the queue is empty.
summary: Clears the cache until the next run
```

### TOML

#### Don't

```toml
# The adress of the server.
description = "Checks the lenght of a name"
```

#### Do

```toml
# The address of the server.
description = "Checks the length of a name"
```

### Markdown

#### Don't

```md
The cache is cleared untill the next run.
```

#### Do

```md
The cache is cleared until the next run.
```

### CSS

#### Don't

```css
/* Keeps the lenght of a line short. */
.prose { max-width: 70ch; }
```

#### Do

```css
/* Keeps the length of a line short. */
.prose { max-width: 70ch; }
```

### SCSS

#### Don't

```scss
// Keeps the lenght of a line short.
.prose { max-width: 70ch; }
```

#### Do

```scss
// Keeps the length of a line short.
.prose { max-width: 70ch; }
```

### HTML

#### Don't

```html
<img src="map.png" alt="The adress on a map">
```

#### Do

```html
<img src="map.png" alt="The address on a map">
```
